name: Saffron
summary: The world's most precious spice, harvested from the stigmas of Crocus sativus. A small pinch transforms rice, sauces, and desserts with golden colour and honeyed fragrance.
description: Saffron threads carry a honeyed, floral fragrance and impart an unmistakable golden hue. The high price reflects labour-intensive harvesting: each flower yields only three stigmas, and every harvest is done by hand. A little goes a long way — steep threads in warm liquid before using to unlock their full colour and flavour. Quality saffron should smell intensely floral, not musty. Deep red threads with orange tips indicate freshness.

pairings.note: A classic Persian pairing — together they define the scent of celebration in rice dishes and pastries.
Earthiness from cumin balances saffron's sweetness in slow-cooked dishes and pilafs.
